footnotes: Notes:— I. Attention is called to the following differences in the length of term of various years given in this return: (a) 13 months ending December 31st, 1868, (b) 9 months ending September 30th, 1869, (c) 12 months ending September, 30th, 1870, (d) 13 months ending October 31st, 1871, (e) 14 months ending December 31st, 1872, (f) 6 months ending June 30th, 1875, (g) 9 months ending March 31st, 1886. The rest consist of 12 months each, the years from 1875-76 to 1884-85 ending on June 30th and the others on March 31st.

II. The figures for the years from 1868 to 1899 are those of the settled accounts, and the figures for 1899-1900 those of the accounts made on November 30th, 1900. The figures relating to the years 1900-1901 and 1901-1902 are taken from the Budgets.

footnotes: Note:— Land tax. Prior to 1872, the expenditures of the prefectures were defrayed directly from the land tax, from 8 % of the land-value officially assessed as the basis of taxation. In 1890, the assessment was but the system came to an end in that year. In 1877, the rate of the land tax was brought down to 2.5 % revised, and in 1899, the rate of the tax was raised from 2.5 % to 3.3 %.
Saké tax. The rate of tax on Saké has been successively raised in the years 1877, 1880, 1896 and 1901.
Soy tax, Income tax. The rates of taxes on soy and income were raised in 1899.
Fishery dues in Hokkaido. The fishery dues in Hokkaido were transferred to the local taxation in 1901.
Tobacco tax. Duties on patent medicines. The tax on tobacco was converted into a leaf-tobacco monopoly, and the duties on patent medicines into stamp duties in 1899.
Customs duties. The rates of the Customs duties were raised in 1899.
